newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel ploughs ahead with settlement plans.
newsitem.headline: Israel ploughs ahead with settlement plans.

text.p: The Israeli government published a newspaper advertisement on Tuesday offering about 120 houses for sale in 30 Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

A Housing Ministry spokesman said the homes were the first of some 3,000 empty housing units which the government decided last October to sell to the public as part of its policy to expand existing settlements.

The sale offer was certain to stir Arab anger, two days before Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was due to hold a summit with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at the Erez crossing between Israel and Gaza.
The previous Labour-led government, defeated by right-wing Likud party leader Netanyahu in elections last May, had frozen the sale.
"A large number of houses needed renovation and about 120 have now been freed up (for sale)," the spokesman said.
The advertisement in the mass circulation Maariv daily was reminiscent of settlement campaigns launched in the 1980s by previous Likud governments.
"You can build on this ad," it said, listing the names and telephone numbers of 30 settlements in which the ministry said private homes were available.

The PLO has called Israel's settlement policy, which includes tax breaks and other financial benefits for Israelis living in the West Bank, Gaza and Golan Heights, a violation of its peace deals with the Jewish state.
Washington has described the outposts as obstacles to peace.

The ministry spokesman said that in addition to the 3,000 empty homes in settlements, the ministry had finalised a previously announced plan to market land in the West Bank and Gaza for the private-sector construction this year of about 5,000 housing units.
He stressed that none of the plans envisaged construction outside of existing settlements.
"We do not think all 5,000 will be sold but estimate the number will be around 3,000," the spokesman said.
The plan, he said, was in line with government decisions and had been approved by Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, whose permission is needed for construction in settlements.
More than 130,000 Jews have settled among some two million Arabs in the West Bank and Gaza since Israel captured the areas in the 1967 Middle East war.
